headline_marked: US envoy and Iranian minister [[head to Switzerland for talks]]
headline: US envoy and Iranian minister head to Switzerland for talks
summary: The meeting follows a ceasefire in Lebanon, reviving efforts to turn an interim Iran war pact into a lasting regional deal.
details: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi are traveling to Switzerland for critical talks. Witkoff will join Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law, who is already in the country.

The diplomatic push comes as a ceasefire in Lebanon between Israel and Hezbollah appears to have revived efforts to secure a lasting regional deal. This follows a 14-point memorandum signed earlier this week to halt fighting.
The talks aim to open a 60-day window to resolve disputes over Iran's nuclear program and other thorny issues. A permanent truce is a primary goal of these technical negotiations.

The broader interim deal requires the U.S., Iran, and their allies to permanently terminate military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. However, Israel has stated it is not a party to this deal.
The regional war, which began on February 28, has killed at least 7,000 people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. It also caused global inflation by disrupting oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
With the ceasefire in place, oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have picked up, and Brent crude prices have seen a weekly fall of about 8%.
caption:

The talks aim to open a 60-day window to resolve disputes over Iran's nuclear program and other thorny issues. A permanent truce is a primary goal of these technical negotiations.

The broader interim deal requires the U.S., Iran, and their allies to permanently terminate military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. However, Israel has stated it is not a party to this deal.

The regional war, which began on February 28, has killed at least 7,000 people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. It also caused global inflation by disrupting oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

With the ceasefire in place, oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have picked up, and Brent crude prices have seen a weekly fall of about 8%.

headline_marked: Walton [[exports motherboards to US]] for security equipment
headline: Walton exports motherboards to US for security equipment
summary: The Bangladeshi tech giant is supplying Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBA) for advanced gunshot detection and emergency rescue systems in the United States.
details: Walton High-Tech Industries has begun exporting motherboards, specifically Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBA), to the United States. These components will be used in high-tech security devices within the US.
The exported motherboards are designed for advanced gunshot detection and emergency rescue operation systems. The importer is SafePro Technologies Inc., a tech firm based in Wisconsin, USA.

The shipment ceremony was inaugurated by Fakir Mahbub Anam, Minister for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, and Rehan Asif Azad, ICT Advisor to the Prime Minister, at Walton's headquarters in Chandra, Gazipur.
Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam praised the achievement, stating that Walton has proven Bangladesh's capability to produce world-class modern technological products for the global market.

Walton currently exports a wide range of 'Made in Bangladesh' products, including refrigerators, TVs, ACs, laptops, and mobile phones, to over 55 countries across Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, and America.
The company's state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities are located in Kaliakoir, Gazipur, where they produce a diverse array of home and electrical appliances, as well as lifts and compressors.
